entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Second supplementary affidavit filed by counsel for the applicants is taken on record.
2. Heard Ms. Abhilasha Singh, counsel for the applicants; Sri Gambhir Singh, counsel for the informant and learned AGA for the State.
Perused the material on record.

3. This application has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.159 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304-B, 201 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Dhanari,
District- Sambhal, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: Counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants were not chargesheeted by the Investigating Officer.
The applicants have been summoned by the trial court vide order dated 3.8.2024 passed under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
The applicants no.1, 2 and 3 are brothers-in-law and applicants no.4, 5 and 6 are sisters-in-law of the deceased.
There are vague and general allegations against the applicants.

The husband of the deceased has been granted regular bail by this Court vide order dated 11.2.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.3848 of 2022 (Ram Kumar vs.
State of U.P.).

entities.text:
Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.3848 of 2022 (Ram Kumar vs.
State of U.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that at the time of incident the applicants were living separately.
In this regard reliance has also been placed on the cross-examination of the informant.
The informant has stated that the deceased and her husband were living separately at NOIDA.
The investigation has been completed.
The applicants had cooperated in the investigation.
The applicants have no criminal antecedents.
The applicants have apprehension of their arrest in the above mentioned case.
In case, the applicants are released on anticipatory bail, they will not misuse the said liberty.
5. Learned A.G.A. as well as counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.

6. Having regard to the submissions made by counsel for the parties and after perusal of the record,
this Court prima facie finds that there are vague and general allegations against the applicants.
In the cross-examination, the informant had stated that the deceased and her husband were living separately at NOIDA.
The husband of the deceased has been granted regular bail by this Court.

Further, the applicants have no criminal history and also that the applicants had cooperated in the investigation, without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicants are entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
7.
8. In default of any of the conditions, the court concerned is at liberty to pass appropriate orders for enforcing and compelling the same.
9. The application stands disposed of.

In the event of arrest, the applicants Chetendra, Devendra, Jugendra, Smt. Asha, Vimla and Anita,
involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on anticipatory bail during pendency of trial, on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) the applicants shall make themselves available on each date fixed in the matter by the court concerned;
(ii) the applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court;
(iii) the applicants shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if they have passport the same shall be deposited by him before the concerned court.
8. In default of any of the conditions, the court concerned is at liberty to pass appropriate orders for enforcing and compelling the same.
9. The application stands disposed of.
